bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 68-byte radio witness drives OpenThread's leader-side Server Data registration path and supplies a Thread Network Data Prefix TLV whose encoded prefix length expands to 25 bytes under `BitVectorBytes(...)`. During `Leader::RegisterNetworkData` and later `AddPrefix`, OpenThread calls the vulnerable `PrefixTlv::IsValid()`, but that helper only checks TLV-internal length consistency and never enforces the patch's missing bound `BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) <= sizeof(Ip6::Address)`. On the fresh leader instance created by the harness, leader network data contains only commissioning data, so `AddBorderRouter` finds no matching stored Prefix TLV, allocates a new Prefix TLV and BorderRouter TLV in `mTlvs`, and copies the malformed prefix length and BorderRouter entry into that persisted state. The later `Mle::HandleStateChanged -> Dhcp6Client::UpdateAddresses` refresh iterates on-mesh prefixes, and `NetworkData::GetNextOnMeshPrefix` executes `memcpy(&config.mPrefix.mPrefix, prefix->GetPrefix(), BitVectorBytes(prefix->GetPrefixLength()))` on stack local `config`. For this witness the byte count is 25, so the copy overruns the 16-byte `config.mPrefix.mPrefix` field and writes 1 byte past the 24-byte stack `otBorderRouterConfig` object, matching the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 25 at `network_data.cpp:138`. The fixing commit tightens `PrefixTlv::IsValid()` with exactly that missing upper bound, so the malformed prefix would be rejected during registration before `AddBorderRouter` can persist the bad prefix state and before `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA` reaches the crashing DHCP6 refresh.

source.code: SuccessOrExit(error = RlocLookup(aRloc16, rlocIn, rlocStable, aTlvs, aTlvsLength, kMatchModeRloc16, /* aAllowOtherEntries */ false));
source.description: First direct project-side consumption of the attacker-controlled Thread Network Data TLV payload on the vulnerability path. Leader registration starts parsing the raw network-data byte span that came from the received Server Data message.
source.value_from: The exact staged 68-byte `poc` is injected as `frame.mPsdu` into `otPlatRadioReceiveDone`. After OpenThread's radio, IPv6, CoAP, and Thread TLV parsing, `Leader::HandleServerData` extracts a valid `ThreadNetworkDataTlv` from the message and forwards `networkData.GetTlvs()` / `networkData.GetLength()` as `aTlvs` / `aTlvsLength` into `RegisterNetworkData`.
source.note: This source is the first bug-relevant project statement after the earlier packet/container parsing has admitted a Thread Network Data TLV.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The current attacker-controlled Prefix TLV entry inside `aTlvs`; its stored `mPrefixLength` field is the tainted value later expanded by `BitVectorBytes(...)` into the 25-byte copy span.

sink.description: ASan sink. `GetNextOnMeshPrefix` copies `BitVectorBytes(prefix->GetPrefixLength())` bytes from the stored malformed Prefix TLV into the stack-local `otBorderRouterConfig config`, but the destination field `mPrefix.mPrefix` is only a 16-byte IPv6 address.
sink.note: Stage 01 reproduces `WRITE of size 25` here. Because `config` is a 24-byte stack object and `mPrefix.mPrefix` starts at its beginning, the 25-byte memcpy overwrites 9 bytes beyond the 16-byte address field and 1 byte past the end of `config` itself.

root_cause.description: Executed admission check that lets the malformed Prefix TLV survive registration. In the vulnerable commit, `PrefixTlv::IsValid()` only checks TLV-internal length consistency and does not require `BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) <= sizeof(Ip6::Address)`, so an oversized prefix length still passes validation.
root_cause.note: The fixing diff adds `&& (BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) <= sizeof(Ip6::Address))` inside `PrefixTlv::IsValid()`. With that extra conjunct, this `VerifyOrExit` would reject the witness before `AddNetworkData` persists the prefix and before `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA` triggers the later crash.

parser_admitted.description: The received CoAP Server Data message has already passed Thread TLV lookup and `networkData.IsValid()`, so execution now enters leader-side network-data registration on the attacker-controlled Thread Network Data TLV payload.

fresh_leader_state.description: The harness creates a fresh `otInstance` for each input and immediately calls `otThreadBecomeLeader()`. `BecomeLeader()` resets leader network data to `mLength = 0` and then `SetEmptyCommissionerData()` seeds only a Commissioning Data TLV, so no stored Prefix TLV exists before the attacker frame reaches Server Data registration.

fine_trace.code:
SuccessOrExit(error = RlocLookup(aRloc16, rlocIn, rlocStable, aTlvs, aTlvsLength, kMatchModeRloc16,
                                     /* aAllowOtherEntries */ false));
fine_trace.note: Source. Leader registration begins validating the attacker-controlled Thread Network Data TLV byte span `aTlvs` / `aTlvsLength` that was extracted from the received Server Data message.
The current network-data entry is reinterpreted as a `PrefixTlv`, exposing its attacker-controlled `mPrefixLength` and prefix bytes to the leader-side validator.

Root cause. This executed admission gate accepts the malformed prefix because vulnerable `PrefixTlv::IsValid()` only requires the TLV length to cover `BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength)` plus header bytes; it does not enforce the fixed bound `BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) <= sizeof(Ip6::Address)`.

The same weak `PrefixTlv::IsValid()` predicate is evaluated again on the storage path. Because it still lacks the `BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) <= sizeof(Ip6::Address)` bound, the malformed prefix is not rejected before `AddBorderRouter` runs.

Fresh-state miss. The staged harness delivers the frame to a new `otInstance`; `BecomeLeader()` resets leader netdata to `mLength = 0`, then `SetEmptyCommissionerData()` seeds only a commissioning-data TLV. `FindPrefix` returns only `kTypePrefix` matches, so no stored prefix matches the attacker bytes here; `dstPrefix` stays `NULL`, and the guarded `FindBorderRouter(...)` assignment is skipped so `dstBorderRouter` remains `NULL`.

Because `dstPrefix == NULL`, AddBorderRouter reserves a new Prefix TLV payload sized as `sizeof(PrefixTlv) + BitVectorBytes(aPrefix.GetPrefixLength())`. For this witness the derived prefix span is 25 bytes, the same tainted copy size later used at the crash.

A new leader-side Prefix TLV is inserted at the end of `mTlvs`. `Init` stores the oversized `mPrefixLength` and copies the corresponding 25 prefix bytes, materializing the malformed prefix state later re-read by DHCP6 iteration.

Because step 5 left `dstBorderRouter` at its initialized `NULL`, the function allocates a new BorderRouter TLV behind the stored prefix, grows the prefix/sub-TLV lengths, and copies the incoming `BorderRouterEntry` into leader `mTlvs`. That copied entry is what the later iterator matches before the sink copy.
After storing the malformed prefix and copied BorderRouter entry in leader network data, registration signals `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA`, exposing that persisted state to later consumers.
The network-data change notifier reaches MLE state handling and triggers DHCPv6 address refresh; the saved ASan stack directly witnesses this caller above the crash.

UpdateAddresses iterates on-mesh prefixes into local stack `otBorderRouterConfig config`. ASan identifies this stack object at line 78 occupying `[48,72)`, so `&config` is the exact destination later overrun.
The overload used by `UpdateAddresses` forces `aRloc16` to `Mac::kShortAddrBroadcast`, so any BorderRouter entry stored under the malformed prefix is eligible for copying into `config`.

The stored leader bytes are reinterpreted as a Prefix TLV again. `prefix->GetSubTlvs()` reuses the oversized `mPrefixLength` from step 7 to skip the stored 25-byte prefix span, and the length growth from step 8 makes `subEnd = cur->GetNext()` cover the persisted BorderRouter TLV and copied entry. There is still no `BitVectorBytes(prefix->GetPrefixLength()) <= sizeof(Ip6::Address)` check before the copy path.

The inner loop skips any non-BorderRouter sub-TLVs until it reaches the stored `BorderRouterTlv`, then reads the copied `BorderRouterEntry` from step 8. Because step 12 fixed `aRloc16` to broadcast, the first matching BorderRouter entry immediately makes the stack copy path reachable.

Destination extent. The callee clears the 24-byte stack `config` object; within it, `aConfig->mPrefix.mPrefix` is only a 16-byte `otIp6Address`, so the next memcpy targets a smaller field than the whole object.

Sink. For this witness `BitVectorBytes(prefix->GetPrefixLength())` is 25, matching ASAN's `WRITE of size 25`. The copy starts at the 16-byte `mPrefix.mPrefix` field inside 24-byte stack `config`, so it overwrites 9 bytes past that field and 1 byte past the end of `config`, producing the reported stack-buffer-overflow write at `network_data.cpp:138`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the overflowing destination as local stack object `config` at line 78, occupying `[48,72)` in this frame.

cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The saved ASan stack directly matches fine-trace steps 10-16 (`Mle::HandleStateChanged -> Dhcp6Client::UpdateAddresses -> NetworkData::GetNextOnMeshPrefix`). Earlier admission and persistence steps 1-9 are reconstructed from the staged vulnerable source and the fixing `PrefixTlv::IsValid()` patch: `Leader::HandleServerData` is the sole `RegisterNetworkData` call site, `RlocLookup()` and `AddPrefix()` are the two executed `PrefixTlv::IsValid()` gates on this path, and the fresh-instance harness plus `MleRouter::BecomeLeader()` reset explains why `FindPrefix` misses before `AddBorderRouter` allocates the stored malformed prefix and copied BorderRouter entry.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The fixing commit adds `&& (BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength) <= sizeof(Ip6::Address))` to `PrefixTlv::IsValid()`. Both executed admissions in this path (`RlocLookup()` and later `AddPrefix()`) would then reject the witness's oversized prefix before `AddBorderRouter` can allocate/store it and before line 797 signals `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA`, preventing the later crashing DHCP6 refresh.

poc.trigger: Running the exact staged 68-byte `poc` under the Stage 01 vulnerable ARVO workspace reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` with `WRITE of size 25` in `ot::NetworkData::NetworkData::GetNextOnMeshPrefix`, matching the saved issue stack through `ot::Dhcp6::Dhcp6Client::UpdateAddresses` and `ot::Mle::Mle::HandleStateChanged`.

format.name: OpenThread radio receive frame bytes
format.contract: The trigger contract is the exact 68-byte witness staged at `gt_results/arvo_13334/poc`. Stage 01 verified that this byte sequence, when passed as `frame.mPsdu` to `otPlatRadioReceiveDone`, reaches leader-side Server Data registration, admits a Prefix TLV whose `BitVectorBytes(mPrefixLength)` evaluates to 25, and later makes `GetNextOnMeshPrefix` memcpy 25 bytes into stack `otBorderRouterConfig config`. No narrower packet-level predicate was recovered from the staged artifacts, so the contract is intentionally limited to this exact witness.
